sketches.title: The Excuse That Got Away
sketches.premise: You and your boss trade excuses for being late. Start with a small, believable excuse; each turn adds one plain detail that makes the same excuse harder to defend. The boss may sound dry, but the excuse is the thing on trial.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the move adds exactly one new detail caused by the last detail and still supports the same excuse; a skipped link is a sudden wild fact, an ending is a complete defense or confession, and an undo is removing or denying a detail already stated.
sketches.move_shape: Say one new fact beginning with “Then,” and leave a fresh problem for the other player to explain. Example: “Then the bus driver stopped to let a duck cross.”

sketches.title: Please Explain This to the Boss
sketches.premise: You build one late excuse by passing it through a chain of people: you, a coworker, a manager, and the boss. Each move gives the next person one exact thing to question, report, or misunderstand. Keep the excuse alive while making its trip upward more awkward.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that each move is the next spoken response from the named person to the last statement; a skipped link jumps past a speaker, an ending settles the excuse or sends the player away, and an undo changes a report already made.
sketches.move_shape: Write one reply from the next person, beginning with “Then [person] said...” Example: “Then the coworker said the pigeon had a badge.”
sketches.first_card: You told your coworker that the train stopped.

sketches.title: The Receipt Department
sketches.premise: You tell the boss why you are late while the boss asks for proof. Each turn adds one ordinary piece of evidence: a ticket, message, photo, or object. The evidence should help at first, then become wonderfully unhelpful.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that each move adds one new piece of evidence that could result from the last claim; a skipped link produces proof with no source, an ending proves the case or destroys it completely, and an undo makes an earlier item vanish or mean the opposite.
sketches.move_shape: Add one item beginning with “Then I showed...” and say what it reveals. Example: “Then I showed a bus ticket stamped 8:40.”
sketches.first_card: You said a bus delay made you late.

sketches.title: The Long Way to the Desk
sketches.premise: You explain your lateness by tracing your path from home to the boss’s desk. Each move moves one place and adds one small obstacle or choice. The route may become ridiculous, but it must remain one walk, ride, or trip toward work.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the move reaches the next nearby place because of what just happened and keeps the traveler heading to the desk; a skipped link jumps across places, an ending reaches the desk or leaves the route, and an undo sends the traveler back or removes a stop.
sketches.move_shape: Name the next place and one event there, beginning with “Then I reached...” Example: “Then I reached the corner, where a delivery cart blocked the crossing.”

sketches.title: Your Calendar Is Testifying
sketches.premise: You and the boss build one day from a calendar entry to your late arrival. Each turn adds one appointment, reminder, or small change that makes the schedule more revealing. The calendar cannot lie, but it can be painfully vague.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that each move adds the next time-stamped event caused by the last calendar item and keeps one continuous day; a skipped link jumps over time, an ending reaches work or closes the day, and an undo changes or deletes a time already established.
sketches.move_shape: Add the next event with a time, beginning with “Then, at [time]...” Example: “Then, at 8:15, the reminder said ‘bring the thing.’”

sketches.title: Three People Saw It
sketches.premise: You give the boss an excuse for being late while witnesses add what they noticed. Each turn introduces the next witness or the next detail from the same scene. Their accounts should fit, but they do not need to make you look clever.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that each move is the next witness’s plain observation caused by the last observation and remains in the same late-morning scene; a skipped link introduces a witness without a reason, an ending gives a final verdict or clears the scene, and an undo contradicts or erases a stated sighting.
sketches.move_shape: Add one observation beginning with “Then [witness] noticed...” Example: “Then the doorman noticed your umbrella was open indoors.”
sketches.first_card: The doorman saw you arrive late.
